notes: Dates: “op 1 mei” = on 1 May.
Say: negentienhonderdnegentig.
u heeft (or u hebt); hij heeft.
“nodig hebben” = to need: “ik heb een diploma nodig”.
Modal verb: the other verb goes to the end as infinitive.
Polite: “Kunt u …?”
Modal verb: infinitive at the end. “Mag ik …?” = May I …?
Modal verb: “ik wil graag werken” – infinitive at the end.
Can also take a noun: “ik wil koffie”.
Modal verb: the other verb goes to the end.
Used for promises and the future: “ik zal het doen” = I will do it.
Infinitive goes to the end.
Used with a negative + te: “je hoeft niet te komen” = you don't have to come.
In a question with jij: “hoef je …?”
“gaan + infinitive” = going to: “ik ga rusten”.
Also part of separable verbs: dichtgaan, ingaan.
“pijn doen” = to hurt: “mijn voeten doen pijn”.
Part of separable verbs: meedoen (doe … mee), opendoen (doe … open).

doe.form: present, ik (here part of meedoen / opendoen)

notes: “de bus nemen” = to take the bus.
